uncited: TangoGS operates on the set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$ defined by the parent [Parent].
The method manages the population size through three phases: allowance calculation, budgeted densification with soft pruning, and final selection.
*   Capture metadata: number of images $N_{\text{img}}$ (including held-out), mean track length, sparse model point count.
*   Training metrics: mean per-image PSNR $P$ from the preceding epoch.
*   A pruned subset of Gaussians $\mathcal{G}_{final}$ with size $N_G$.
*   Densification starts at 2% of total training iterations.
*   Soft pruning begins at ~9% of total training iterations.
*   Densification ends at 80% of total training iterations.
*   Keep the top fraction $\rho$ of Gaussians.
*   Let $N_{\text{pre}}$ be the population entering this event.
*   Rank all $N_{\text{pre}}$ Gaussians by sensitivity score.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Significantly lower than standard 3DGS and baselines like LeGS.
*   **When to use:** When deploying 3DGS on diverse captures without manual hyperparameter tuning.
*   **When not to use:** When strict real-time training constraints prohibit the sensitivity score accumulation or when capture metadata is unavailable.
It builds on LiteGS for sensitivity scoring and integrates with standard 3DGS optimization.

TangoGS is a density control strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting that automatically scales the number of Gaussian primitives to match the complexity of the input capture without per-scene tuning [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that TangoGS is a density control strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting. It confirms that the method automatically scales the number of Gaussians based on capture-derived metrics (model sizing) and training-based adaptation (quality feedback), thereby matching the complexity of the input. Furthermore, the evidence highlights that TangoGS uses a shared configuration across all captures and does not require per-scene tuning, unlike baselines.
